title: Pollination
examples: What is the difference between pollination and fertilization?
Can wind pollinate flowers that are deep inside a plant?
How does a bee get pollen stuck to it?

explain.say: Today we are learning about pollination in plants. Pollination is the movement of pollen.

items: Pollen moves from anther to stigma

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the parts of a flower. Look at the petal, the sepal and the anther. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Bees are very important pollinators for many plants. They carry pollen on their fuzzy bodies.
Wind is another way pollen can travel. Wind carries very light pollen grains over distances.
Flowers have parts that help with pollination. The anther holds the pollen, and the stigma receives it.
After pollination, fertilization happens inside the flower. This mixes pollen with the ovule.
Fertilisation leads to the development of seeds. Seeds contain the baby plant for the future.

faq.q: What is the difference between pollination and fertilization?
faq.a: Pollination is when pollen moves from one flower to another. Fertilization is the actual joining of the pollen with the ovule inside the flower.
asks: What happens after pollen lands on a flower?
Is pollination the same as fertilization?

faq.q: Do all flowers need insects to pollinate them?
faq.a: No, some flowers are pollinated by wind or even by water. The flower has different adaptations for different methods.
asks: Can plants be pollinated without bees?
What are other ways pollination happens?

faq.q: How does the seed get ready to grow?
faq.a: The seed develops after fertilization inside the ovary of the flower. It needs certain conditions to start growing.
asks: What does a seed need to germinate?
Where does the seed come from?

faq.q: What part of the flower catches the pollen?
faq.a: The stigma is the sticky part of the flower that is designed to catch pollen grains. It is the receiving end.

faq.q: If a plant is pollinated by wind, what does that mean for the flower?
faq.a: It means the flower does not need bright colors or sweet smells to attract animals. It relies on the air movement instead.
asks: Why do some flowers smell sweet?

facts: Pollen contains the male reproductive cells for the plant.
Bees are attracted to flowers by nectar and scent.
Wind pollination often involves producing large amounts of light pollen.
Fertilization is the process that starts the seed development.

quiz.say: A bee moves pollen from one flower to another. This process is called:
quiz.why: This describes the physical transfer of pollen between flowers.

wrong.0: This is how the plant makes its own food using sunlight.
wrong.2: This is the joining of cells inside the flower, not the movement of pollen.
wrong.3: This is when the seed starts to grow, which happens later.

quiz.say: Which method of pollination is best suited for very light, dusty pollen?
quiz.why: Wind carries light particles over long distances when there is enough air movement.

wrong.0: Water is usually too slow or requires a body of water to move pollen.
wrong.1: This is too general; wind is the specific force for light pollen.
wrong.3: Bees are good for sticky, visible pollen, not necessarily very light dust.

quiz.say: If pollen lands on the stigma, what must happen next for the plant to make seeds?
quiz.why: Fertilisation is the necessary step that combines the pollen with the ovule.

wrong.0: Growth happens later, after the seed has formed.
wrong.1: Absorption is taking in nutrients, not the reproductive process.
wrong.3: Pollination is just the landing; fertilization is the internal action.
